title: Fast triage handbook for VPC / on-prem installs
body:
PURPOSE
This is a compact, pragmatic triage handbook for first responders on VPC and on-prem installations. It focuses on the fastest evidence-gathering steps, known failure fingerprints observed during 2023–2025 installs, and safe next actions (fixes, mitigations, or rollbacks). Use this as the 0–90 minute play for an install/runtime incident.

SCOPE
- Applies to Private (VPC and on-prem) installs of Redwood control plane + runtime packages using the official terraform modules and our installer.
- Assumes operator shell access to at least one bastion or admin node with kubectl / terraform and access to cloud console or on-prem IPMI/BMC.

QUICK PATH (0–15 min) — collect the minimum evidence
1) Confirm customer symptom and scope: which cluster/region, single node vs multi-node, time window.
2) Check installer/terraform exit status on the operator machine:
   - cat ~/redwood-install/logs/install.log | tail -n 200
   - terraform -chdir=terraform-state plan -no-color 
     (look for provider errors and 'inconsistent object' messages)
3) Node health (from bastion):
   - ssh admin@node-01 'sudo systemctl is-active redwood-runtime || sudo systemctl status redwood-runtime --no-pager'
   - ssh admin@node-01 'journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200 --no-pager'
4) Networking quick sanity:
   - ip a | grep -E "ens|eth|bond"
   - ip route show default; ip route get 8.8.8.8
   - ping -c3 controlplane.internal.local (DNS + routing quick check)
   - curl -sS https://metadata.service.internal/health || echo METADATA_FAIL
5) Terraform state and locks: 
   - terraform -chdir=terraform-state state list | wc -l
   - check for lingering locks: terraform -chdir=terraform-state force-unlock -list
6) K8s quick (if control plane up):
   - kubectl get nodes --no-headers -o wide
   - kubectl -n redwood-system get pods -o wide | head -n 50

FAST HYPOTHESES (ranked)
- H1: Networking/DNS misconfig preventing bootstrap or registration. Symptoms: timeouts to API endpoints, repeated TLS handshakes, pods stuck in ContainerCreating with imagepull backoff.
- H2: Terraform provider/api rate limits or partial apply left resources in bad state. Symptoms: partial infra present, dependencies failing in installer.
- H3: Kernel / NIC driver mismatch on on-prem hosts (MTU/BGP/ARP asymmetry). Symptoms: cluster nodes flapping, high packet loss, BGP sessions resetting.
- H4: Systemd service OOM or permission failure (KMS/HSM access blocked). Symptoms: redwood-runtime crashloop with permission denied or HSM errors.

DEEP DIVE (15–90 min) — targeted checks and mitigations
A) Networking & DNS
   - Verify MTU consistency across all datapath interfaces: sudo ip link show; compare MTU values.
   - Check iptables/nftables rules created by customer infra that may DROP traffic to 9000–9010 (runtime ports).
   - Use tcpdump on the controlplane interface while retrying registration: sudo tcpdump -n -i ens+ 'host <control-ip> and port 9010' -c 200
   - DNS: dig +trace controlplane.internal.local; confirm SRV/A records and TTLs
   - Quick mitigation: add static /etc/hosts entries for controlplane to bypass DNS for bootstrap (only as temporary)

B) Terraform / State integrity
   - Inspect drift: terraform -chdir=terraform-state plan -detailed-exitcode || capture output. Exit 2 indicates diff.
   - Look for errors from cloud provider SDKs in the install.log (429/503). If rate-limited: pause concurrent applies, retry with exponential backoff.
   - If backend lock persists and operator confirmed no other apply in progress: terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>

C) Runtime logs (examples and signatures)
   - Common: "kv cache init timeout after 30s" → often caused by incorrect path or missing persistent volume. Check PV/PVC in Kubernetes: kubectl get pvc -n redwood-system
   - Common: "HSM: unable to open session: CKR_DEVICE_ERROR" → HSM/KMS config or permissions; check mounts, sockets, and env VARS fed to service.
   - Common: "gpus: allocate failed: driver mismatch" → NVIDIA driver mismatch; sudo nvidia-smi to confirm GPU presence and driver version.

SAMPLE LOG FINGERPRINTS (for quick grep)
- Permission / file issues: "permission denied" OR "EACCES"
- Networking: "connection refused" | "i/o timeout" | "TLS handshake failure"
- Cloud infra: "API rate limit exceeded" | "RequestLimitExceeded"
- Kernel OOM: "Out of memory" followed by "OOM kill" in dmesg

QUICK FIXES (when safe)
- DNS: add temporary host override and re-run installer registration steps.
- PV missing: recreate PVC from snapshot or attach the correct storage class.
- HSM credentials invalid: rotate credentials in installer secrets and restart systemd service.
- Driver mismatch: for pilot/test, switch runtime to CPU-only variant in the config to get control-plane fully healthy before scheduling GPU work.

UPGRADE PREFLIGHT CHECKS (before any terraform apply or module upgrade)
- Backups: snapshot terraform state, export db backups for control plane (s3 or NFS)
- Telemetry snapshot: curl -sS http://localhost:9090/metrics | head -n 200 
- Run the upgrade dry-run: terraform -chdir=terraform-state plan -var-file=upgrade-vars.tfvars -out=upgrade.plan
- Confirm change set contains only allowed diffs (no destructive replacement of PVs or KMS keys)
- Confirm rolling-update policy: ensure maxUnavailable and maxSurge are configured to avoid full outage

ROLLBACK / SAFE STOP
- If upgrade breaks control plane: scale down new components and re-apply previous plan artifact: terraform apply upgrade-rollback.plan
- For runtime crashloops: systemctl stop redwood-runtime; set systemd to manual start and leave it down until escalation if crash cause is unknown

ESCALATION CRITERIA
- If crash persists after restarts + obvious config fix (15–30min) escalate to eng-serving-runtime and include the full log bundle and terraform plan output.
- If data integrity at risk (PV rebind/recreate) stop further changes and page oncall infra for snapshot recovery.

VERIFICATION SNIPPETS (copy-paste)
- Collect systemd + journal in one go: sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 1000 --no-pager > /tmp/redwood-runtime.journal && tar czf /tmp/troubleshoot-logs.tgz /tmp/redwood-runtime.journal /var/log/cloud-init.log /var/log/syslog
- Kubernetes: kubectl -n redwood-system get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 50
- Terraform last apply: terraform -chdir=terraform-state show -json > /tmp/last-apply.json

KNOWN EDGE CASES & WORKAROUNDS (from field)
- BGP / MTU mismatch between leaf switches and host bonding caused segmentation on 1500-sized frames — workaround: temporarily set link MTU to 1400 and re-run verification. Long-term: fix switch config.
- Private registry TLS handshake fails due to intermediate CA missing — workaround: add CA to /etc/ssl/certs and restart container runtime.

POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS
- Save a triage timeline in the incident ticket: key commands run, outputs and timestamps, people involved.
- Capture a minimal reproducible failure repo: config diffs and smallest repro steps.
- File follow-up for infra fixes (switch config, driver upgrade) and a runbook tweak if necessary.

NOTES & REFERENCES
- Keep a short log bundle and attach to JIRA ticket. Use the linked_artifacts above for relevant terraform PRs and runbook pages.
- If stuck: reach out on #private-deployments with incident tag and include the short bundle.

APPENDIX (useful commands summary)
- terraform -chdir=terraform-state plan -out=plan.bin
- terraform -chdir=terraform-state show -json plan.bin | jq '.'
- sudo tcpdump -i any port 9010 -c 200 -w /tmp/capture.pcap
- sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime && journalctl -u redwood-runtime -f

END - keep this doc short and copy-friendly; drop sections into an incident ticket as needed.
